MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  APRIL 18, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:04 p.m. in the City Council Chambers at Rolling Hills
  Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by
  CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  and Retz (joined at 6:12 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  Romanelli

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF MARCH 21, 2022

  VICE CHAIR BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MARCH 21, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  Stephanie Yinger, the new Community Relations Manager of South Coast Botanic
  Gardens introduced herself and noted upcoming events at the Gardens, including
  a Cirque Du Soleil sponsored egg hunt, an upcoming show titled “Soar,” and
  “Flamboyance – A Topiary Menagerie” opening May 1st.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
APRIL 18, 2022
   **ITEM 7C. TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  C.  SPECIAL EVENT PROPOSAL - STRIDES IN RECOVERY 5K

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ joined the meeting at 6:12 p.m.

  Jenna Campbell of Strides in Recovery was in attendance.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if this was the organization’s first 5k event.
  Jenna Campbell responded that they plan to hold a 5k walk in June but that this is
  the organization’s first 5k race. He asked how the 200-300 runner estimate was
  calculated. Jenna Campbell responded that her director, Leslie Gold, would be
  proactive in advertising the event.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE APPLICATION FOR STRIDES IN RECOVERY’S USE OF
  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AND THE CITY’S 5K RACECOURSE TO HOST
  THEIR EVENT ON SEPTEMBER 18, 2022, UNDER THE CONDITIONS
  AND FOR THE FEES OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  6.  PARK TOUR

  A.  CHANDLER PARK

  The Commission toured Chandler Park including the area for the proposed play
  equipment but refrained from conducting a formal discussion regarding the
  proposed playground structure until reconvening back at the chamber.
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith commented on planned
  improvements to the Chandler Arena.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLAYGROUND STRUCTURE AT CHANDLER PARK - UPDATE

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA thanked staff for the survey.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
APRIL 18, 2022
   CHAIR CIAROLLA opened the floor for public comments.

  Resident Pam Schachter commended staff on the survey, the time allowed to
  complete the survey, and the scope of its reach. She expressed concern for those
  in favor of play equipment, stating that many commented they wanted more
  equipment such as swing sets and slides. She shared that she is on the
  subcommittee, which agreed there would be no slides or swings, and only low to
  the ground equipment to climb on. She commented that she does not like the
  location of the playground as it is away from the public eye and pushed into a
  corner. She added that hikers meeting at the park have made horses nervous as
  the horses cannot see what they hear and that it makes the horses upset. She does
  not approve of a slide or swing set for the playground.

  Linda Belton of Torrance shared that she has been a rider for over 30 years. She
  expressed concern about the horses as they are creatures of flight when scared
  and alarmed. She noted an incident at Ernie Howlett Park where football players
  and frisbees were thrown in her direction and her horse spun to avoid them. She
  commented that people with horses must deal with strollers, bikes and homeless
  on the trails. She added that signs are ignored, and loose horses may cause
  accidents. She commented that screaming and yelling of children cannot be
  controlled and the use of other rings requires travelling through tunnels to access
  and that those rings are already busy. She commented that horses are different by
  day and a playground may cause accidents.

  Resident Lyneigh Palacios shared that she is in support of the playground. She
  thanked staff for the survey commenting that it was well done with qualitative and
  quantitative results. She shared that she is a 25-year resident of the City who lives
  about half a mile from Chandler Park and that her views went from neutral to in
  support of playground due to public health concerns. She stated that the family that
  brought the park proposal is a newer stakeholder, and the needs of the new and
  old stakeholders should be balanced with consideration of the views of the new
  stakeholders. She commented that the approval process is long and frustrating for
  some. She commented that a past meeting formed a subcommittee that invited
  those from the Roanwood and Ranchview neighborhoods but that the City should
  have reached outside of the area. She added that she was a two-minute drive or
  12-minute walk away from the invited sections and was not invited. She stated the
  survey comments saying to drive to Rockbluff Park, or another park did not consider
  those nearby and that some did not get mailers due to address issues sending
  letters to PV Estates. She stated that the park is a great asset for kids under 5
  walking to another school with low profile equipment and that she would like to see
  conceptual plans and agrees with risk to the equestrian community and favors risk
  mitigation with horses. She added that the City may need to bring in someone from
  outside the equestrian community to help assess the situation and that all sports

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
APRIL 18, 2022
   have risks and riders should be responsible for their own safety. She noted past
  issues with off-leash dogs from the equestrian community.

  Resident Rich Oldroyd stated his opposition to the playground equipment. He
  stated that he raised his daughter near Chandler Park, that he appreciates its wide-
  open grass area, and that he likes the quiet park. He commented that Ernie Howlett
  Park has ADA compliant play equipment and has amenities for patrons. He stated
  that he is worried that if every park has play equipment, the green space will be
  lost. He stated that Chandler Park is not a good place for young children’s
  equipment.

  Resident Jackie Alonso commented that she would like to see action taken as it
  has taken two years so far and that she would like to see action taken on this
  proposal.

  Resident Jim Marziani stated that he is a longtime resident of the area. He thanked
  staff on the progress made on this proposal. He stated that he likes the natural part
  of the city and that the horse overlay zone is nice for him. He commented that open
  space is important as he comes to park every day and he likes when children are
  enjoying nature as it is. He stated that he would not like to lose a park that has no
  play equipment. He noted the survey showed more people in favor of the play
  equipment, but more people spoke against it tonight in person.

  Nancy Maholski of Rancho Palos Verdes stated that she boards her horse at Peter
  Weber Equestrian Center. She commented that she appreciates the equestrian
  community in this city and has observed that boarders have doubled during her time
  here. She stated that if more rings were within Peter Weber Equestrian Center
  (PWEC) this would not be an issue, but the Chandler Park ring is needed by the
  boarders and that the safety factor is worth considering.

  ACM Davis shared that written public comments had been received by email and
  had been forwarded to the Commission prior to the start of the meeting. ACM Davis
  read the emailed comments from residents Vicki Shinn and Jeremy and Jackie
  Alonso into the record (the comments are attached to this document).

  CHAIR CIAROLLA closed public comments.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the amount of equipment, and that the placement is
  appropriate for the park. He stated that he does not own horses but rides and has
  neighbors who ride. He commented that having play equipment in view of horses
  versus out of view of horses has been brought to equestrian community and wanted
  to know the results of their findings.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA responded that horses prefer to see where sounds are coming
  from so as not to get spooked. She commented that if it is decided by the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
APRIL 18, 2022
   Commission that staff continue to investigate installing the equipment, she would
  suggest installing fencing around the play equipment so that children could not run
  at the ring towards the horses. She asked community member Pam Schachter for
  her opinion. Pam Schachter said the fencing may take away from the open green
  space in park.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that small children are already playing at the park
  and that she has not heard of any incidents of children rushing to the ring up to this
  point. She thanked staff for their hard work on this project and the community for
  their input and concern. She stated that she feels there is a compromise and is
  inclined to more research. She commented that the concerns she read were
  primarily safety considerations. She noted a comment from Vicki Shinn that there
  may be ways to get the playground to work by addressing those concerns such as
  putting the playground in line of site of the ring and placing it away from trail with
  signage. COMMISSIONER POPE added that signage may benefit the playground
  and address safety concerns. She added that the compromise for families that
  want bigger structures would be to build something not as big as Ernie Howlett
  Park’s play structure adding that small children cannot play at Ernie Howlett Park
  with the bigger children there. COMMISSIONER POPE commented that small
  equipment is a compromise and the compromise for those with the desire to keep
  green space is the proposed natural looking play structures like logs and rocks as
  opposed to putting in concrete or brightly colored plastic equipment. She added
  that extending a child’s engagement with nature is a better alternative than having
  them play in nearby canyons.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK commented that he was impressed with the
  survey responses. He noted a high percentage of families that would use the park
  more with more amenities. He stated that as a parent of young children, there is a
  need for more interaction in the park that would benefit the children physically and
  emotionally. As a member of the subcommittee, he noted the compromise of less
  noisy park equipment was made for horse safety.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN noted this was the first time she heard the idea of adding rings
  to the PWEC to offset use of Chandler Park and asked staff to investigate the
  PWEC concept. She commented that signage, location of the park, and low-profile
  equipment for small children would not raise a safety issue in her opinion. ACM
  Davis responded that space is limited at PWEC. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith added that Ernie Howlett Park has five rings and PWEC has no room for
  more rings. ACM Davis noted that there was a proposal from the PWEC to add a
  ring to the PV Landfill for a program, but the land belongs to Los Angeles County
  and staff will investigate that possibility.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a recommendation to approve play
  equipment at Chandler Park.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
APRIL 18, 2022
   COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there was a second to the recommendation.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the recommendation could still be modified with a
  second motion.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN expanded the recommendation to include low profile play
  equipment for small children and that it be presented to the community with more
  detail than provided in the survey adding that she would like to make that
  recommendation to City Council.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated she would also like to add to the recommendation
  that safety concerns be addressed, and that staff consider the placement of the
  play equipment.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN added that the fencing and brush clearance near the playground
  by PV Drive North be addressed as well.

  ACM Davis clarified the recommendation to consider play equipment for small
  children addressing safety concerns, with placement consideration, attention to
  fencing and brush clearance, and signage to educate the public on horse behavior
  for families with small children per Commissioner Pope’s suggestion.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  RETZ to:

  CONSIDER CHANDLER PARK PLAY EQUIPMENT FOR SMALL
  CHILDREN ADDRESSING SAFETY CONCERNS, WITH PLACEMENT
  CONSIDERATION,  ATTENTION  TO  FENCING AND  BRUSH
  CLEARANCE, AND SIGNAGE TO EDUCATE THE PUBLIC ON HORSE
  BEHAVIOR FOR FAMILIES WITH SMALL CHILDREN.

  AYES: Bain, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz

  NO: Ciarolla

  ABSENT: Romanelli

  The motion carries.

  B.  RECREATION FEES REVIEW

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the Tracy Austin Tournament fees were low
  compared to other city’s fees.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
APRIL 18, 2022
   ACM Davis noted tournament workers and players mentioned the low pricing point
  of the tournament compared to others.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted the price was low for the tournament
  compared to what was offered and that the $4.00 increase per player is a good
  start. ACM Davis noted there is room to increase the price and another review of
  the pricing could be done next year.

  VICE CHAIR BAIN asked if the pickle ball fees would be the same as those for the
  tennis players. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that those
  fees have not been established yet and would be established later after first being
  brought to the tennis facility subcommittee.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE CITY’S RECREATION
  FEES TO THE CITY COUNCIL.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz

  ABSENT: Romanelli

  The motion carries.

  D.  ESTABLISHMENT OF TENNIS FACILITY SUBCOMMITTEE
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONERS ROMANELLI, MCCORMICK, and PERSICHINA were chosen
  to join the subcommittee.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  NONE.

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted Dapplegray Park looked good.
  VICE CHAIR BAIN commended the fencing at Highridge Park. Maintenance

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
APRIL 18, 2022
   Superintendent Goldsmith noted the cutouts and walkthroughs. VICE CHAIR BAIN
  asked to install electric hand dryers as the women’s hand towel dispenser is broken
  and creates unnecessary trash with paper towels. She also observed that the area
  for turf removal can be expanded. She added that the mural looks great and is
  better than expected. ACM Davis stated that her suggestions of electric hand
  dryers would be taken into consideration.
  VICE CHAIR BAIN noted the completed mural at Highridge Park and asked if the
  bulletins were finished. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that
  the artist would finish the bulletin boards that week and noted plans to hold a
  ribbon cutting ceremony in April.
  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)
  NONE.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MARCH 22, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 12, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  NATURE CENTER UPDATE

  NONE.

  B.  BUTCHER PARK UPDATE

  NONE.

  12.  PARK TOURS

  A.  PEPPERWOOD PARK, SILVER SPUR PARK AND ROCKBLUFF PARK
  CHAIR CIAROLLA noted that because of the time and lack of daylight, the Silver
  Spur Park, Rockbluff Park, and Pepperwood Park tours would be rescheduled to
  another date due to limited visibility.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
APRIL 18, 2022
   13.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:43 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON MAY 16, 2022, AT
  6:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  9
APRIL 18, 2022
